attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his essay, written as his prediction.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with no hedge. Scoping it to Facebook and Instagram matches the surrounding sentence. Leaving out the separate prediction about content that riles users up is appropriate. No horizon was given.

contract.note: 'As much as it wants' gives no quantity. Reading it as a substantial expansion of promoted AI content on both platforms is an ordinary, fair plain reading. Requiring an irreversible event before contradicting it fits a forecast with no deadline.

evidence.note: Sept 2025 Meta disclosure: a Vibes AI-video feed in the Meta AI app, with cross-posting to Instagram and Facebook Stories and Reels. It shows tools and direction but no measured feed promotion on both platforms.
Sept 2024 disclosure that predates the forecast. It shows AI-image sharing and feed tests already existed, so it is a baseline, not fulfilment.
Apr 2025 Facebook crackdown on spam distribution. It is not specific to AI content and is not a permanent bar, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows Meta building AI-content tools and cross-posting (Vibes), but no measured, substantial expansion of AI content promoted in both Facebook and Instagram feeds. The spam crackdown is not an irreversible bar. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met, so it stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his essay.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense claim that AI slop dominates Facebook. Separating it from the claims about Meta's motives and platform quality is appropriate.

contract.note: The speaker named no measure. Reading 'dominates' as a majority of feed exposures is an ordinary plain reading. Jan 1–17, 2025 is a reasonable evaluator-chosen window for 'already'. The result depends on that threshold and window.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study of 125 deliberately selected AI-image pages, from 2024. It gives no platform-wide feed share and covers a period before the target window.
A June 2024 single-account feed test found AI content was 22% of posts. Different period, not representative, so context only. It does not support majority prevalence.

reviews.rationale: No representative measurement of Facebook feed exposures for January 2025 is in the packet. The available items are a selected-page study and a single-account test from 2024 that found 22%. Both cover a different period and are not representative, so neither establishes or refutes a majority share in the target window.
